extracted.intended_audience: President and Council of Fort St. George; East India Company senior administrators and colonial officials
extracted.subtask_description: Formal instructions and principles issued by the Board of Control and Court of Directors for arranging the surrender of revenue assignments, settling the Nabob's debts, prescribing treaty terms, and regulating administration, repairs, and revenues in the Carnatic (late 18th-century colonial governance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rajah's liability limited to admitted government share
rubrics_metrics.description: Our opinion being that the Rajah ought to be answerable for no more than the amount of what he admits was collected by his people for the government share of the crop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not compel the Rajah to pay supposed balances or render a specific account beyond what he admits; if the deposit's proper application is unclear, suspend application of the deposit until fully explained and further orders received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling deposit from Rajah re: Nabob's claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rajah has actually paid into our treasury one lac of pagodas, by way of deposit, on account of the Nabob's claims to the crop, till our sentiments should be known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surcease any further demands from the Rajah on that account and, if local difficulty arises in disposing of the deposit consistently with principles of justice, suspend application and report for further orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration and treatment of assignees' claims (Mr. Benfield etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your government recommended to the Rajah to restore to Mr. Benfield the grain of the last year ... and to give Mr. Benfield all reasonable assistance in recovering such debts as should appear to have been justly due to him from the inhabitants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether parts of the government share taken by Rajah's people were included in amounts the Rajah admits; ascertain any compensation made to assignees; if unclear, local government should apply deposit consistently with justice or seek further orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anicut and Cavery banks repairs — customary practice and regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: It appeared perfectly reasonable that the Rajah should be permitted to repair those banks, and the Anicut, in the same manner as had been practised in times past; and we directed you to establish such regulations, by reference to former usage, for keeping the said banks in repair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to prior investigations and reports; establish regulations effectual to remove future complaints; repeat orders where necessary; if repairs are more expensive with local materials, seek permission from the Nabob to use Trichinopoly materials and obtain lease of spots for sand/earth at reasonable rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of materials for repairs and conditional leases
rubrics_metrics.description: If ... expedient, you apply to the Nabob ... that his Highness will permit proper spots of ground ... on the Trichinopoly side, where the Rajah and his people may at all times take sand and earth ... and that his Highness will grant his lease of such spots of land for a certain term of years to the Company, at a reasonable annual rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose lease to secure cultivation without impairing Nabob's rights; lease should remain no longer in force than while Rajah is punctual in payment of annual peshcush and reserved rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of Company engineers for repairs
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be recommended ... that skilful engineers, appointed by the Company, be employed at the Rajah's expense to conduct all the necessary works, with the strictest attention to the respective rights and interests of both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineers appointed by Company, acting under Madras government appointment; immediate redress for either party via application to government of Madras to avoid disputes between parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender of assignment and principle of moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: We have resolved that the assignment shall be surrendered; and we do accordingly direct our President, in whose name the assignment was taken, without delay, to surrender the same to his Highness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While surrendering, adopt heads and principles of arrangement to secure British interests and preserve Nabob's dignity; proceed from principle of moderation and to cement harmony and confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soucar security: twelve lacs of pagodas annual instalments for debt liquidation
rubrics_metrics.description: That, for making a provision for discharging the Nabob's just debts ... the Nabob shall give soucar security for the punctual payment, by instalments, into the Company's treasury, of twelve lacs of pagodas per annum, until those debts, with interest, shall be discharged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry into execution by a formal deed between his Highness and the Company; the arrangement is to be bonâ fide and to be enforced according to resolutions and determinations made under legislative provision for liquidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to Bengal government on soucar security disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Should any difficulty arise ... in respect to the responsibility of the soucar security, or the times and terms of the instalments, it is our pleasure that you pay obedience to the orders and resolutions of our Governor-General and Council of Bengal in respect thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defer to Supreme Government of Bengal for determinations in such disputes; expect Nabob to abide by their determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve right to demand additional security on default
rubrics_metrics.description: We reserve to ourselves full right to demand of the Nabob such additional security, by assignment on his country, as shall be effectual for answering the purposes of the agreement, in the event of the failure of the security proposed, or in default of payment at the stipulated periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No specific assignment proposed initially, but Company will insist on additional security if payments/defaults occur, to protect Company and private creditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaty principle: joint contributions to military support
rubrics_metrics.description: All the contracting parties shall be bound to contribute jointly to the support of the military force and garrisons, as well in peace as in war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treaty(s) should bind parties to specified contributions; military peace establishment to be settled by Company in pursuance of parliamentary authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securing contributions by specifying districts and revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nabob and Rajah must ... specify particular districts and revenues for securing the due and regular payment of their contributions into the treasury of the Company ... with power for the Company, in case of failure or default of such payments ... to enter upon and possess such districts, and to let the same to renters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Couple this power with positive assurance of Company's determination to support the Nabob's and Rajah's dignity and exclusive administration of civil government and revenues; use entry/possession only on stipulated default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue application during war and civil establishment protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Company ... shall engage to refrain, during the war, from the application of any part of their revenues to any commercial purposes whatsoever, but apply the whole, save only the ordinary charges of their civil government, to the purposes of the war ... that the sum be now ascertained which is indispensably necessary to be applied to those [civil] purposes, and which is to be held sacred under every emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine and set apart the sum for civil establishment before applying revenues to defence; aggregate revenue to be under Company application during war and thereafter as necessary to discharge war-contracted burdens, but without depriving Nabob/Rajah of substantial authority to collect revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company accounting obligation while administering revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: The Company are to engage, during the time they shall administer the revenues, to produce to the other contracting parties regular accounts of the application thereof to the purposes stipulated by the treaty, and faithfully apply them in support of the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce regular accounts to demonstrate faithful application; transparency intended to maintain confidence among contracting parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of Nabob's and Rajah's troop numbers and Company aid
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nabob shall ... agree not to maintain a greater number of troops than shall be necessary for the support of his dignity and the splendor of the durbar, which number shall be specified in the treaty; and if any military aid is requisite ... the Company must be bound to furnish him with such aid: the Rajah of Tanjore must likewise become bound by similar engagements, and be entitled to similar aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify troop numbers in the treaty; Company to provide military assistance for security and revenue collection where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting renters/lessees to hold leases to term or indemnify
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the Nabob ... for his consent that they may be permitted to hold their leases to the end of the stipulated term ... but if ... his Highness should be impressed with any particular aversion to comply ... you must take especial care to give such indemnification to the renters for any loss they may sustain as you judge to be reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek Nabob's consent; if refused, do not insist but ensure reasonable indemnification to renters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for faithful natives in authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Such natives as may have been put in any degree of authority over the collections ... and who have proved faithful to their trust, shall not suffer inconvenience on account of their fidelity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that those natives who served faithfully under the assignment are not penalized as part of the settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diplomacy and prudence in official communications
rubrics_metrics.description: We earnestly recommend that those opinions and speculations be communicated to us with prudence, discretion, and all possible secrecy, and the terms in which they are conveyed be expressed in a manner as little offensive as possible to the powers whom they may concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use address, civility, conciliation before measures that could offend the Nabob; avoid offensive language and preserve secrecy and discretion in communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and treatment of 1767 consolidated debt
rubrics_metrics.description: In speaking of the loan of 1767, we are to be understood as speaking of the debt as constituted by the original bonds of that year, bearing interest at 10_l._ per cent ... if any creditors ... claim the benefit of the following orders ... we direct that you pay no regard to such claims, without further especial instructions for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the 1767 consolidated debt as constituted by original bonds at 10% interest; do not extend benefits to later higher-interest bonds purporting to be part of 1767 without special instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious recognition of 1777 consolidated debt and review of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The loan of 1777 ... has no sanction or authority from us; ... we so far adopt the general presumption in their favor as to admit them to a participation in the manner hereafter directed, we do not mean to debar you from receiving any complaints against those debts of 1777 ... and if any complaints are offered, we order that the grounds of all such be attentively examined by you, and be transmitted to us, together with the evidence adduced in support of them, for our final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admit 1777 debts to participate in distributions subject to careful local examination of complaints and transmission of evidence to the Board for final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution rules for the twelve lacs of pagodas (order of application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The debt consolidated in 1767 to be made up to the end of the year 1784, with the current interest at ten per cent. The Cavalry Loan to be made up to the same period, with the current interest at twelve per cent. The debt consolidated in 1777 to be made up to the same period, with the current interest at twelve per cent, to November, 1781, and from thence with the current interest at six per cent. The twelve lacs annually to be applied: 1. To the growing interest on the Cavalry Loan, at twelve per cent. 2. To the growing interest on the debt of 1777, at six per cent. The remainder to be equally divided: one half to be applied to the extinction of the Company's debt; the other half to be applied to the payment of growing interest at 10_l._ per cent, and towards the discharge of the principal of the debt of 1767.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the precise schedule and priorities given; continue arrangement until the principal of the 1767 debt is discharged; after Cavalry Loan discharged, adjust sums (seven lacs to Company's debt, five lacs to 1777 growing interest/capital) and ultimately apply all to discharge 1777 when others cleared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of additional payments (Tanjore peshcush) to Company's debt
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Nabob shall be prevailed upon to apply the arrears and growing payments of the Tanjore peshcush in further discharge of his debts, over and above the twelve lacs of pagodas, we direct that the whole of that payment, when made, shall be applied towards the reduction of the Company's debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional voluntary payments from Nabob to be earmarked for reducing Company's debt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion and punitive measures for non-acquiescent creditors
rubrics_metrics.description: If any creditor of the Nabob, a servant of the Company, or being under our protection, shall refuse to express his acquiescence in these arrangements, he shall not only be excluded from receiving any share of the fund under your distribution, but shall be prohibited from taking any separate measures to recover his debt from the Nabob ... and if any creditor shall be found refractory, or disposed to disturb the arrangement we have suggested, he shall be dismissed the service, and sent home to England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require creditors under Company's protection to acquiesce; enforce exclusion from fund and remove/punish servants who disturb the settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No protection for unsanctioned new debts to British subjects until investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The directions we have given only apply to the three classes of debts which have come under our observation. It has been surmised that the Nabob has of late contracted further debts: if any of these are due to British subjects, we forbid any countenance or protection whatever to be given to them, until the debt is fully investigated, the nature of it reported home, and our special instructions upon it received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not protect or recognize newly alleged debts to British subjects without full investigation and instructions from the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Company servants engaging in loans with country powers
rubrics_metrics.description: We hereby ... repeat our prohibition upon this subject, and direct that no person, being a servant of the Company, or being under our protection, shall, on any pretence whatever, be concerned in any loan or other money transaction with any of the country powers, unless with the knowledge and express permission of our respective governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strictly enforce the 1714 prohibition; send offenders home to England to be punished and give no protection for recovery of such loans; any connivance will incur highest displeasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of peace and respect to Nabob and family
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nabob has complained that no official communication was made to him of the peace, for near a month after the cessation of arms took place. This, and every other mark of disrespect to the Nabob, will ever appear highly reprehensible in our eyes; and we direct that you do, upon all occasions, pay the highest attention to him and his family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely and respectful official communications to the Nabob and his family; avoid actions or omissions that may be construed as disrespectful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Praise and censure of officials' conduct standards
rubrics_metrics.description: We cannot dismiss this subject without expressing our highest approbation of the ability, moderation, and command of temper with which our President at Madras has conducted himself ... While we find so much to applaud, it is with regret we are induced to advert to anything which may appear worthy of blame: as the step of issuing the Torana Chits in Lord Macartney's own name can only be justified upon the ground of absolute necessity ... more of [address, civility, conciliation] might have been used; and therefore we cannot consider the omission of it as blameless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials should exercise ability, moderation, command of temper, and prefer conciliatory means before measures that could be offensive; justify extraordinary steps only upon clear necessity and after attempting less offensive approaches.
